To: Cloudflare Workers Support, through the private support channel for SHIFT account 9e5386dcf455be34c582d93f8bfc79e6
Subject: SHIFT shift-core: registered Cron Trigger has no observed scheduled execution after guarded release
Body:
Hello Cloudflare Workers Support,

Please investigate the Cron Trigger registration and dispatch for account 9e5386dcf455be34c582d93f8bfc79e6, Worker shift-core, expression */15 * * * *. The Worker is serving version ca5ca696-3fa1-47bc-b1d7-85a2d6d587f9 at 100% under deployment 45868df4-c841-4ad2-949d-ef91ebd83689, created 25 October 2026 at 20:17:19 UTC. Its published handlers include fetch and scheduled. Ordinary authenticated member journeys, the expected database binding and schema, and the serving-version identity have been verified.

Our original schedule was modified on 14 October 2026 at 19:39:09 UTC, during your activation incident npjny9agana8. Your resolution noted that some affected schedules might require redeployment. This is a temporal correlation; we cannot confirm it caused this account's missing executions.

An idempotent schedule update at 21:02 UTC retained the old timestamp. We therefore removed and recreated only this same registration at 21:04:19 UTC, checking the exact serving deployment before and after. The registration now has that new creation/modification time. We changed no Worker code, route, binding or cadence and did not force or replay a business job.

As of 25 October 2026 at 21:33 UTC, none of our ten Core job keys has written a startup/completion row. This includes the 21:30 slot, more than 25 minutes after the registration was recreated. The exact serving version was rechecked before and after the read. A communications job scheduled at 20:40 UTC reached the immediate job-recording entry point at 21:29:15 UTC and completed at 21:29:19 UTC, approximately 49 minutes late. Its code captures the start timestamp before database I/O. This establishes delayed handler entry for that invocation; the platform's internal cause remains unknown.

Independent communications and support Workers have actual scheduled completion records. One support run scheduled at 20:50 UTC recorded its start at 21:13 UTC and completed at 21:13:11 UTC. This proves lateness, rather than completion of every scheduled slot. Our telemetry queries find ordinary Core fetch traffic but no Core scheduler log or durable job record in the observed window. The GraphQL Cron Events endpoint also omitted known communications runs, so we are not treating that endpoint alone as proof of no execution.

Please check the active registration-to-Worker mapping, Cron dispatch and any account-specific backlog or activation problem. Advise a provider-side repair that preserves the current serving version, routes, bindings and existing 15-minute cadence. Please do not run duplicate business jobs, change credentials, purchase support or otherwise make a charge or commitment on our behalf. No secrets, patient information or member payloads are attached.

Thank you,
Matt
